clue.text: Unpleasant characters dismissing leader of harness racers

indicators.note: dismissing the leader means the first letter of the racers' word is sent away

parts.note: trotters are horses that race in harness, pulling a light cart

explanation.surface: A grumble about the shady folk who hang around harness racing, with the boss of the stables sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotters is a dated British term of abuse for nasty, contemptible people.

clue.text: Ornate four-poster, no end of usage, safe against certain decay

indicators.note: ornate suggests elaborately reworked, signalling the letters are rearranged
no says a letter is missing from the pool before rearranging
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An elaborate four-poster bed, barely used, protected against rot.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E (the end of usage) out of FOURPOSTER and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustproof means protected from rust, the particular corrosion that attacks iron and steel.

clue.text: Vulgar business, tucking into stewed rodent in old part of Turkey

indicators.note: tucking into means the business word goes inside the mixed letters
stewed means cooked up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: biz is a slangy, informal word for business

explanation.surface: A crude trade involving eating stewed rat in a historic region of Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vulgar' marks the slangy short form of business. Trebizond, now Trabzon, was a medieval empire on the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Trebizond was a medieval Greek empire on Turkey's Black Sea coast, now the city Trabzon.

clue.text: Make up for old head contains iodine

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: contains means the head word holds the iodine symbol

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: Compensating an old man whose head has been dosed with iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin is to atone for it, which means compensating for the wrong done.

clue.text: Piece about simply ignoring the odds? It could make you a packet

definitions.text: It could make you a packet

indicators.note: about means the piece word goes round the even letters

parts.note: a shard is a broken piece, as of pottery

indicators.note: dropping the odd-placed letters of the word keeps the even ones

explanation.surface: A tip-off that a simple bet ignoring the odds could earn you a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet is a packet boat, a ship carrying mail; 'make you a packet' sounds like earning a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipyard is where ships are built, and a packet was a regular mail-carrying ship.

clue.text: Tricky maths with introduction of algebra leads to complaint

indicators.note: tricky suggests something awkward and twisted, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A pupil finds hard maths, made worse once algebra starts, brings on illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment or illness, and asthma is one such medical condition.

clue.text: Second channel covering Duke's outrage

indicators.note: covering means the channel word goes over the Duke's letter

parts.note: a canal is a man-made channel
D is the abbreviation for Duke; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A second TV channel reporting a Duke's disgraceful conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A scandal is an outrage, an event provoking public shock and indignation.

clue.text: Entertain our group in garden

indicators.note: in means our group's word sits inside the gardening word

parts.note: to hoe is to work a garden
us is the group that includes the speaker

explanation.surface: An invitation to host our party out in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To house guests is to put them up, giving them hospitality in your home.

clue.text: Skilful elevation of soft pedal to some extent

indicators.note: in a down clue elevation raises the letters, so they read from bottom to top
to some extent means only part of the phrase is used, the letters hiding in it

explanation.surface: A pianist is skilled at lifting the soft pedal a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means expert, highly proficient at something.

clue.text: Youngster accepting tip of lapel as component of suit

indicators.note: accepting means the youngster word takes in the letter

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior scout

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A young boy taking hold of the edge of a jacket lapel that forms part of his suit.
explanation.walkthrough: The suit is in cards, not clothes: a club is a card of the clubs suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs are one of the four card suits, so each club card is a member of that suit.

clue.text: Shelter in special surroundings for a nap

indicators.note: in places the shelter word inside the other piece
surroundings says the special abbreviation encloses the shelter word

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: Finding a sheltered spot in a special setting to have a quick doze.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short period of slumber, so it can be called a sleep.

clue.text: Working laser unlit, out of singular spite

indicators.note: working means set in motion and rearranged, signalling the letters are shuffled
out of says a letter must be taken away from the shuffled pool

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Someone flicks on a laser that was off, out of sheer malice.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove S from LASER UNLIT and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill nature is a spiteful, malevolent disposition, so it matches malice of that kind.

clue.text: Expensive to go round V&A, having the place to yourself?

definitions.note: a phrase describing the state rather than a noun, with the question mark admitting it

indicators.note: to go round means the costly word encloses the museum's letters

parts.note: pricy means costly
the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, shortened to its letters V and A

explanation.surface: A costly private tour of the V&A museum, getting the galleries all to yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Privacy is the state of being alone and unobserved, which is what having somewhere to yourself gives.

clue.text: Be about to say more linked to telco financial woe

indicators.note: about means the word Be wraps around the other piece

parts.note: to add is to say something further
BT is British Telecom, the UK's main telephone company

explanation.surface: A phone company boss is about to speak further about the firm's money troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is the former British Telecom, Britain's big telephone company.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad debt is a loan that will never be repaid, a classic money problem for a lender.

clue.text: Old structure on top of mosque, say — attempt measure of distance

parts.words: structure on top of mosque, say
parts.note: a dome crowns many mosques, the 'say' showing it is an example
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: An old builder tries to work out how far it is to the dome atop a mosque.
explanation.definitionFit: Odometry is the measuring of distance travelled, as done by a vehicle's mileage counter.

clue.text: Recording's about to fail, admitting of no further discussion

indicators.note: about means the recording's letters go round the failing word

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording; the 's stands for 'is'
to lose is to fail to win

explanation.surface: A recording is going wrong, and the matter cannot be debated any more.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed question or subject is settled, with debate over and no more argument allowed.

clue.text: Suggestion corps in error will have to work on farm area

indicators.note: in means the corps letter goes inside the error word

parts.note: a sin is a wrong, an error
C is an abbreviation for corps, as in military unit names
to till is to work the land

explanation.surface: A military unit that went wrong is told to labour on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny trace or hint, so it means the barest suggestion of something.

clue.text: Passed round spread on view

indicators.note: round means the dying word goes round the spreading word

parts.note: to pass away is to die
splay means spread out

explanation.surface: A dish was handed round the table, a spread for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something displayed is exhibited, put out where people can see it.

clue.text: Dreadful sin in start of the Bible? Not the start

indicators.note: in means the sin word goes inside the other pieces
the start of a word is its first letter
not the start means the opening letter of the holy book is dropped

parts.note: to err is to sin

explanation.surface: Is the first sin in the Bible really so awful? Not at the beginning, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' is used twice: first to pick a letter, then to say a letter is dropped from the holy book.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrible and dreadful are synonyms, both meaning extremely bad.

clue.text: Fellow I had to hire is a restless type

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
to get someone is to take them on, as when hiring

explanation.surface: An employer says they had to take on a man who could never keep still.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidget is a person who keeps making small nervous movements and cannot sit still.

clue.text: European agreement about heritage body without teeth?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective

indicators.note: about means the agreement word goes round the heritage letters

parts.note: a deal is an agreement
the NT is the National Trust, which looks after historic buildings in Britain

explanation.surface: A European deal about a heritage body that has no real power.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity caring for historic houses; 'without teeth' sounds like a powerless agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Edental is a zoological adjective for animals lacking teeth, a variant of edentate.

clue.text: Energy lacking in distribution of ice-creams in pots

indicators.note: distribution means the letters are spread about into a new order
lacking means a letter is missing from the pool before it is reordered

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tired server hands out ice creams in tubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E from ICECREAMS and rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceramics are pottery items, so pots is a general term for them.

clue.text: Bending over, possibly demonstrating hiding head

indicators.note: hiding the head means the first letter is kept out of sight

parts.note: protesters may march, so marching is one way of demonstrating

explanation.surface: Stooping protesters who keep their faces covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Arching means curving into a bow shape, as when the body bends over.

clue.text: Concern raised about verse getting split

indicators.note: about means the worry word goes round the verse letter

parts.note: care means concern or worry
up means raised, lifted

explanation.surface: Worry is growing over a poem that has caused a rift.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up is a division or sharing out, often an unfair one between parties.

clue.text: Scotsman not excited about University

indicators.note: about means the calm word goes round the university letter

parts.note: calm means not excited

explanation.surface: A Scot stays cool about going to university.
explanation.definitionFit: Calum is a Scottish man's given name, the Gaelic form of Malcolm's root Columba.

clue.text: Inflexible doctor needing documentation

parts.note: to doctor results is to rig them, to falsify
ID is identification papers, documentation

explanation.surface: A stubborn physician who insists on seeing your papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means stiff and unbending, unable to give way.

clue.text: Choice trimmed feathers?

indicators.note: trimmed means the tail end is clipped off

parts.note: a plume is a feather or tuft of feathers

explanation.surface: Selecting which feathers to cut, perhaps for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job or role is a choice one, highly desirable.

clue.text: Subsequently keeping one contralto back for concert

indicators.note: back means the whole result is read in the opposite direction
keeping means the later word holds the other letters

parts.note: later means subsequently
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is an abbreviation for contralto in vocal scores

explanation.surface: Later on, a contralto is held back from performing at a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a musical performance, often by a soloist, so it is a kind of concert.

clue.text: What may illuminate mild recall of unhappy sound?

parts.note: light means mild, gentle

indicators.note: recall here means calling back, so the crying word runs in the opposite direction

parts.note: to blub is to cry, an unhappy sound

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what might shed light on a faint memory of a sob.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric bulb gives out light, so it is something that can illuminate a room.

clue.text: I vote against including large item of decorative woodwork?

indicators.note: including means the vote word holds the large letter

parts.note: nay is a vote against
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone opposes the inclusion of a big piece of ornamental carpentry.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlay is a decoration set into a wooden surface, as in marquetry.

clue.text: Daughters in the distance (not far or near?)

indicators.note: in means the daughters' letters go inside the distance word

parts.note: a mile is a distance
D is the abbreviation for daughter, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Daughters seen in the distance, though not too far off or close.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'middle distance', between far and near.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle ground lies between the far and the near, as in the middle distance of a painting.

clue.text: Country no good as home to antelope? On the contrary

indicators.note: as home to describes one piece housing another
on the contrary flips the housing, so the antelope holds the no-good letters rather than the reverse

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A country is said to be useless as a habitat for antelope, or perhaps the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, NG houses the antelope; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles so ELAND houses NG.
explanation.definitionFit: England is one of the nations of the United Kingdom.
